summary: CRISIS REGIME — BEARISH WITH ENERGY/DEFENSE EXCEPTIONS. The market is in the early innings of a major geopolitical shock. Operation Epic Fury (US-Israel strikes on Iran, Feb 28) has triggered the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which handles 20% of global oil supply. Oil surged 8.5% on March 3 and is heading significantly higher (Brent will reach $100+ within days, eventually $120+ by mid-March). The traditional safe-haven playbook is BROKEN: gold is falling, Treasuries are selling off (yields spiking), and the dollar is strengthening as the market prices a stagflationary energy shock rather than a deflationary risk event. The S&P 500 lost 0.94% on March 3 after being down as much as 2.5% intraday — expect continued volatility with a downward bias. VIX at 23.75 in backwardation confirms near-term fear exceeds long-term, and VIX likely heads to 29+ by March 6. Key dynamic: massive sector rotation FROM tech/discretionary INTO energy/defense. Broadcom earnings tonight are a wildcard — a strong AI beat could provide a temporary lift to semis but won't change the macro picture. The next 2 weeks are critical: if Hormuz stays closed, we get a full-blown energy crisis. If Trump's Navy escort plan works or a ceasefire emerges, rapid de-escalation is possible but unlikely in the near term. Position for continued crisis: long energy/defense, short high-beta tech/consumer/airlines, hedge with VIX calls.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: CRITICAL: On Feb 28, 2026, the US and Israel launched 'Operation Epic Fury' — surprise joint airstrikes against Iran targeting nuclear facilities, military infrastructure, and leadership (Supreme Leader Khamenei assassinated). Over 1,700 sorties struck 1,250+ targets in the first 48 hours. Iran retaliated with missile/drone strikes on US bases, Israeli territory, and Gulf states. IRGC closed the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping traffic — this is the single most important market driver. The war entered its 4th day on March 3. Trump stated March 3 that the US Navy would escort tankers through Hormuz 'if necessary.' Markets swung wildly — S&P was down 2.5% intraday on March 3 before recovering to close -0.94%. Defense stocks surging (NOC +6%, AVRL +10%, LMT +3%). This is a hot shooting war with massive commodity supply disruption — crisis regime is fully justified.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Fed funds rate at 3.5-3.75% (held steady at Jan meeting). FOMC meeting in 14 days (March 18) where they will hold again 11-1. 10Y yield surging to 4.08% (+59bps) as markets price stagflation — rising oil = inflation expectations up, but war/uncertainty = growth fears. The yield curve is positively sloped (2-10 spread +43bps), suggesting markets fear inflation more than recession near-term. Dollar strengthening (DXY 99.32, +0.56%) as flight-to-cash dominates over flight-to-quality. Key: traditional safe haven playbook is BROKEN — Treasuries selling off (yields up) because market is pricing energy-driven inflation shock, not a deflationary bust. NFP in 2 days, CPI in 7 days — both will be pre-war data and largely irrelevant to current crisis dynamics. Real risk: stagflation scenario if Hormuz stays closed for weeks.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: BROADCOM (AVGO) reports Q1 FY2026 after close TODAY (March 4). Consensus expects EPS $1.88, revenue ~$19B. AI revenue expected to be massive — will likely beat given prior quarter trends. This is the biggest single-stock catalyst today. Microsoft (MSFT) closing its worst quarter since 2008 (-23%), as AI spending scrutiny intensifies. Big Tech AI capex expected at $720B in 2026 — 'prove it' era for returns. OpenAI at $25B annualized revenue, Anthropic at $19B. Corporate earnings broadly taking a backseat to the geopolitical crisis — war uncertainty overshadowing fundamentals.

sections.title: Tech
sections.content: Semiconductor sector (SMH +2.06%) showing resilience despite crisis — AI demand seen as secular and war-independent. AVGO earnings tonight are the key catalyst. A major risk: helium shortage emerging from Hormuz closure (critical for chipmaking) — if prolonged, could constrain semiconductor production. Apple targeting AI Siri release with iOS 26.4 in March. Anthropic's Model Context Protocol hit 97M installs. Morgan Stanley warning of an 'AI breakthrough' in 2026 that most aren't ready for. Tech faces a two-way pull: secular AI tailwind vs. crisis-driven rotation out of high-beta growth. Near-term, the rotation OUT of tech into energy/defense is the dominant flow.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: OIL IS THE TRADE. WTI surged 8.5% to $81 on March 3 (up from ~$71 pre-strikes). Brent at $85.41 (+4.93%). The Strait of Hormuz handles ~20% of global oil supply. Iran's IRGC has prohibited vessel passage. Oil prices will continue to surge — Brent eventually hits $120+ by mid-March and $166 (Dubai crude) by March 19. IEA members will release 400M barrels from strategic reserves on March 11, but this only slows the spike. LNG, LPG, naphtha all disrupted. Petrochemical plants curtailing production. Energy stocks (XOM, CVX, COP) up 4-5% on March 3 and have significantly more room to run. Natural gas prices rising in Europe and Asia. This is a supply-driven energy shock with no quick resolution — Hormuz reopening requires either military escort success or ceasefire.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: MAJOR: On Feb 20, SCOTUS ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs, striking down the legal basis for Trump's 2025 tariff regime. A new 10% global surcharge under Section 122 took effect Feb 24 for 150 days. On March 4 (TODAY), Judge Eaton of the Court of International Trade orders CBP to begin IEEPA tariff refunds to importers — this is a mild positive for importers/retailers. New Section 301 investigations launched March 11-12 targeting 16 countries. Net effect: tariff uncertainty remains but the SCOTUS ruling was actually a modest de-escalation on the trade front. The tariff story is now secondary to the Iran war as the dominant policy driver.

scenarios.trade: Oil supply shock is the dominant market narrative. Hormuz handles 20% of global oil — closure means sustained price spike regardless of SPR releases. XOM has diversified upstream/downstream operations, strong dividend, and will generate massive FCF at $80+ oil. Energy stocks rallied 4-5% on March 3 with significantly more upside as oil continues higher. Target reflects WTI reaching $95-100 range within 2 weeks.

scenarios.implication: Rapid ceasefire and Hormuz reopening would collapse oil prices and energy stocks. US Navy escort success could also cap oil upside. A global recession triggered by the oil shock could eventually destroy demand.

scenarios.trade: ConocoPhillips has the highest direct leverage to crude oil prices among large-cap E&P names. Pure upstream exposure means every dollar of oil price increase flows almost directly to the bottom line. At $95-100 WTI, COP's FCF yield becomes extraordinary. The Hormuz crisis is not priced in — markets are still absorbing the implications of a sustained closure.

scenarios.implication: Rapid de-escalation and Hormuz reopening. Oil price collapse below $70 on ceasefire news. Government windfall profit tax rhetoric if oil goes too high.

scenarios.trade: A hot war with Iran means sustained and escalating defense spending. Northrop Grumman is the premier defense contractor for the systems being actively used — B-21 Raider, missile defense, autonomous systems. Congressional appropriations for defense will surge. This is not a one-day trade — defense spending commitments last years. The +6% move on March 3 is just the beginning of a multi-week re-rating.

scenarios.implication: Quick ceasefire reduces urgency for defense spending. Budget deficit concerns limit new appropriations. Profit-taking after initial spike.

scenarios.trade: VIX term structure in backwardation is a strong signal that the crisis is not yet fully priced. The market recovered from -2.5% intraday to close -0.94% on March 3, suggesting complacency that will be punished as the Hormuz situation worsens. NFP in 2 days adds event risk. FOMC in 14 days is a major uncertainty (stagflation dilemma). UVXY provides leveraged exposure to the vol spike. Target assumes VIX reaches 30+ within the week. IMPORTANT: This is a short-duration trade — vol products decay. Take profits quickly.

scenarios.implication: VIX mean-reverts quickly on ceasefire headlines. UVXY decay erodes value even if VIX stays elevated. Market finds a floor and vol compresses.

scenarios.trade: Airlines are the most oil-price-sensitive sector in the market. Jet fuel is 25-35% of operating costs, and the Hormuz closure is sending crude toward $100+. American Airlines specifically has weaker hedging and a weaker balance sheet than peers. Consumer travel demand will also soften as gasoline prices rise and war uncertainty weighs on confidence. The crisis has weeks to run — this is a sustained headwind, not a one-day event. Short penalty is 0 in crisis regime.

scenarios.implication: Quick ceasefire and oil price collapse. Airline hedging programs better than expected. Pent-up travel demand proves resilient despite higher fuel costs.

scenarios.trade: Carnival is a leveraged play on consumer travel and fuel costs — both are moving against it. Bunker fuel is a massive expense, and with Brent heading to $100+, margins get crushed. Additionally, the Middle East conflict directly threatens Mediterranean and Gulf cruise itineraries. Carnival still carries significant post-COVID debt, limiting financial flexibility. Consumer confidence will drop as gasoline prices rise. Zero short penalty in crisis regime.

scenarios.implication: Quick conflict resolution. Oil price pullback on SPR release. Booking data remains strong despite headlines. Cruise demand proves inelastic.

scenarios.trade: Lockheed Martin is the world's largest defense contractor and a direct beneficiary of the Iran conflict. F-35s are central to air operations, and the company's missile and naval systems are deployed in the region. Like NOC, this is a multi-week to multi-month thesis as defense appropriations increase. Lower beta than NOC but more diversified defense exposure.

scenarios.implication: Rapid ceasefire. Defense budget sequestration concerns. Profit margins already at peak levels. Valuation stretched after initial spike.

watchlist.trigger: After-hours earnings report tonight (March 4). If AI revenue beats $8B+ and guidance exceeds $21B, consider long despite crisis regime — AI semis are proving crisis-resistant.
watchlist.reasoning: Broadcom is the single biggest corporate catalyst today. A massive AI beat could temporarily decouple semis from the crisis narrative. Watch the after-hours reaction — if shares rise 5%+ on results, the AI demand thesis is intact and AVGO becomes a high-conviction long even in crisis. If it sells off despite a beat, that confirms the crisis rotation is overwhelming sector-specific catalysts.

watchlist.trigger: If gold stabilizes above $5,000 for 2-3 sessions while yields stop rising, initiate a contrarian long. The traditional safe-haven bid will reassert once the growth shock hits.
watchlist.reasoning: Gold fell despite war — this is the 'inflation trade beats safety trade' dynamic. But if Hormuz stays closed 2+ weeks, growth fears will dominate inflation fears, dollar weakens, and gold becomes the best safe haven. Watch for the inflection point.

watchlist.trigger: If 10Y yield spikes above 4.25% but equity markets break to new lows, consider long TLT as a recession hedge. The bond market will eventually price growth destruction over inflation.
watchlist.reasoning: Treasuries are selling off on stagflation fears, but if the oil shock triggers actual economic contraction, bonds rally hard. TLT at depressed levels with yields above 4.25% would be an asymmetric entry for a recession scenario.

watchlist.trigger: If WTI sustains above $85 for 3+ days, initiate long. Oilfield services lag the oil price move but catch up as producers ramp activity.
watchlist.reasoning: Halliburton benefits from both higher oil prices and increased US domestic production — if Hormuz stays closed, the US government will push hard for domestic output increases, which is Halliburton's bread and butter.

watchlist.trigger: If Hormuz closure is confirmed as lasting more than 1 week with no Navy escort success, add direct oil exposure via USO as a momentum play.
watchlist.reasoning: Direct crude oil exposure via ETF. Only if the crisis deepens and oil heads toward $100. Beware contango decay in normal times, but in backwardation (current state), USO actually benefits from roll yield.

avoidList.reasoning: Down 23% in Q1 2026 — worst quarter since 2008. AI spending scrutiny, high-beta tech in crisis rotation. Falling knife with no clear catalyst for reversal while war continues. Do not try to catch the bottom.

Ultimate high-beta consumer discretionary name. Rising gasoline prices reduce the 'EV value proposition' narrative short-term, while risk-off rotation punishes speculative growth. Elon Musk political controversies add idiosyncratic risk. Avoid both long and short — too unpredictable in crisis.

Caught between two massive forces — secular AI demand (bullish) vs. crisis rotation out of tech (bearish) plus helium supply risk from Hormuz closure threatening chip production. Wait for AVGO earnings tonight to clarify the AI demand picture before taking any position. Too much uncertainty to have conviction either direction.
